Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

category noun

a class or group in a classification

also categories, class (of things), categorize, put into categories, classification

classical

Plin. Ep. 2.6.2: in tria genera discrīpserat
Cic. Ac. 2.7: ūnum genus reprehēnsōrum

genus, generis n.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

kind, class, category

The general word for a class of things or people, its commonest sense in every period (Lewis & Short). Also birth, descent, a race or family, and in grammar gender. In genera dīvidere, discrībere: to sort into categories. For “kind, sort” in everyday talk, see kind.

Other words

  • classis, classis f. — a class (of citizens); a rank

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Ac. 2.73: quīntae classis (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically one of the Servian property classes of citizens, and the fleet; figuratively a rank (philosophers “of the fifth class”, Cic.). Not a general word for a category of things.

  • catēgoria, catēgoriae f. — a category in logic (Aristotle’s ten)

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin · Aug. Conf. 4.16 (Lewis & Short); Isid. Orig. 2.26.1 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Greek κατηγορία: post-classical, and only in logic (the pure Latin is praedicāmenta); also an accusation (Jerome).

Examples

  • Vīnum etiam parvolīs lagunculīs in tria genera discrīpserat, nōn ut potestās ēligendī, sed nē jūs esset recūsandī

    He had even sorted the wine, in little flasks, into three categories, not so that one could choose but so that one had no right to refusePlin. Ep. 2.6.2

See also kind, sort.
